title: UN Security Council — adoption on the Haiti Gang Suppression Force mandate, days before the force's 30 September authorisation lapses
source: EST: onu.diplomatie.gouv.fr/en/french-presidency-security-council-program-work, fetched direct 2026-09-15 (HTTP 200) during the unsc-middle-east-2334-2026-09-28 initial research. The French presidency's 'Provisional Agenda of Work of the Security Council - September 2026' ('as of' 31 August 2026, published 2 September 2026) dates 'Tuesday, 29 September Adoption (A.M.) - Haiti [GSF mandate]'. Secondary sources date the vote a day later: securitycouncilreport.org's September-2026 Haiti forecast and chathamhouse.org (both read 2026-09-15) say the Council votes on renewal on 30 September, which is also when the GSF's own authorisation lapses - resolution 2793 authorised it for an initial 12 months from 2025-09-30, adopted 12-0-3 (abstaining China, Pakistan, Russia). The US and Panama are the co-penholders; the force has asked for an extension through September 2028. Estimate on the one-day primary/secondary discrepancy, on the programme being provisional rather than adopted, and on CONFIRMED_PREFIX carrying no UN slot. Checked 2026-09-15
notes: PROPOSED AS THE ONE DECISION-CLASS ITEM in the French provisional programme that this calendar does not already track. The proposer's own sweep found six other dated slots on that document and filed none of them: 09-23 'Briefing (11:00 A.M.) - TBC' has no named subject; the 09-24 League of Arab States informal interactive dialogue and the 09-25 UNHCR briefing are product-free discussion formats; and the 09-24 UNDOF, 09-25 Colombia and 09-28 OPCW entries are report due-dates, not meetings. This one is different in kind, not in importance: it is an ADOPTION - a scheduled Council vote with a hard mandate expiry behind it - which is the same class this calendar already tracks as unsc-iran-panel-mandate-vote-2026-09-17, and the class that can actually produce a dated outcome. WHY low AND symbols: [] REMAIN THE HONEST FILING: Haiti carries no listed instrument in this book, no commodity channel and no supply chain this calendar touches; the entry earns its place as a corridor date anchor in an already-crowded quarter-end week (PCE 09-30, ISM 10-01, jobs 10-02, funding deadline 09-30), never as a catalyst. The 09-29 vs 09-30 discrepancy is left open on purpose, exactly as unsc-iran-panel-mandate-expiry-2026-09-26 leaves its own 26/27 split open: both candidate days are inside the same week and neither licenses date-keyed action while the entry is an estimate. The event this proposal's own initial research must settle is which date the Council actually adopts on, and whether a 12-0-3 baseline holds with the force asking for two more years.
